## Context

- Interpreter `python` (Python 3.12 target; the bench machine reports 3.14, stdlib only either way). Suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` from the project root; one module: `python -m unittest tests.<module>`. New tests go in `tests/test_<topic>.py` (HOW_WE_WORK.md).
- Money is integer cents everywhere (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md). Member kinds `standard`, `student`, `staff`; every per-kind number lives in `shelf/policy.py` (`KINDS` policy.py:3, `LOAN_DAYS` :5, `MAX_LOANS` :6, `DAILY_FEE_CENTS` :7 = 25/10/0, `GRACE_DAYS = 1` :10, `FEE_CAP_CENTS = 1000` :11, one flat cap for all kinds). Per-kind accessors follow one pattern: `DICT[check_kind(kind)]` (`check_kind` policy.py:14 raises `ValueError("unknown member kind: ...")`).
- `shelf/fees.py`:
  - `late_fee_cents(days_late, kind="standard")` fees.py:5 — grace, daily rate, then `min(..., policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS)` at fees.py:10. This line is the only reader of the cap.
  - `loan_fee_cents(loan, today, kind="standard")` fees.py:13 → `late_fee_cents(loan.days_late(today), kind)`.
  - `format_cents(cents)` fees.py:18 — `f"${cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"`. Bugs today: `format_cents(-5)` gives `$-1.95` (floor division on negatives), `format_cents(123456789)` gives `$1234567.89` (no thousands separator). There is no `parse_cents`.
  - `flat_fee(days)` fees.py:23 — deprecated, no caller; out of scope, leave it.
- Callers of the money code: `LoanDesk.checkin` loans.py:49 returns `fees.loan_fee_cents(loan, loan.returned, kind)` (loans.py:56); `reports.overdue_report` reports.py:7 imports `format_cents, loan_fee_cents` (reports.py:4) and prints `format_cents(fee)`. Existing tests pinning behaviour: `tests/test_basics.py` `FeesTest` (lines 36-54: `late_fee_cents(400) == policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS`, `format_cents(1234) == "$12.34"`, `format_cents(5) == "$0.05"`, unknown kind raises `ValueError`), `tests/test_loans.py:36` `test_checkin_fee` (standard, 25 days after checkout → 75 cents).
- Import graph: `loans` imports `fees` and `policy`; `fees` imports only `policy`. So `fees` must not import `loans` (cycle); functions that need a desk take it as a duck-typed argument (`desk.loans`, `desk.members`, `desk.today()`, `desk.open_loans(member_id)` loans.py:28).
- `LoanDesk` has no payment or balance record; member balances (`balance_cents`, `FEE_BLOCK_CENTS`) arrive in phase 1.5. A fee returned by `checkin` is settled at the desk in this model, so "what a member owes" in this phase is the fee accrued on their open loans as of today.
- Fixture: `tests/helpers.library(clock=None)` helpers.py:41 → `(catalog, members, desk, clock)`: six books, `M0001` standard, `M0002` student, `M0003` staff; `Clock` starts Monday 2024-03-04, `clock.advance(days)`.
- Phase 1.2 (open days) may move due dates onto open days before or after this phase lands; tests here must derive expected fees from `loan.days_late(today)` or from explicit `late_fee_cents` inputs, never from hard-coded calendar arithmetic, so they survive 1.2.
- Phase 1.3 depends on 1.1 (ISBN-13 keys); nothing here touches ISBN code, the dependency is ordering only.

## Rationale

- Three tasks along the milestone's seams: T1 formatting/parsing (pure functions, `tests/test_money.py`), T2 the per-kind cap (policy + one line in `late_fee_cents`), T3 the owe-reports that consume both. T3 depends on T1 (it prints amounts) and T2 (its numbers must be capped per kind). T1 and T2 are independent and may run in either order.
- Format chosen: `-$1,234.56` (sign before the currency symbol, comma thousands groups, always two decimals, `$0.00` for zero). This is the common accounting-free display and the shape `parse_cents` can invert unambiguously. Parentheses for negatives rejected: harder to parse, no caller wants it.
- `parse_cents` accepts exactly what `format_cents` emits plus two conveniences staff scripts will type: no `$`, and no comma grouping (`"1234.56"`). If a comma appears the grouping must be well formed. A decimal point needs exactly two digits after it; no decimal point means whole dollars. Anything else raises `ValueError`. Floats are never used (split on `.` and use `int`), so there is no rounding.
- `format_cents` rejects non-`int` (including `bool` and `float`) with `TypeError`: money is integer cents, and a float slipping in is a bug worth surfacing.
- Cap per kind: new dict `policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS_BY_KIND` and `policy.fee_cap(kind)` in the accessor pattern. `policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS` stays, equal to the standard cap, because `tests/test_basics.py:46` and possibly staff scripts read it. Default values: standard 1000 (unchanged), student 500, staff 1000 (staff's daily rate is 0, so their cap is moot). The student number is money policy, so it is under `## Developer decides`; the plan proceeds with 500 unless told otherwise — the tests assert `late_fee_cents(400, kind) == policy.fee_cap(kind)` and that student's cap is what the dict says, so changing the number is a one-line edit.
- `outstanding_cents` and `fee_summary` live in `fees.py` (money in one module; `reports.py` already imports from `fees`). They take the desk as an argument to avoid the `fees → loans` cycle. Outstanding = sum of `loan_fee_cents(loan, today, kind)` over the member's open loans; returned loans are excluded because their fee was settled at `checkin` (balances are phase 1.5's job). Rejected: counting returned-late loans too — it would double-charge once 1.5 adds balances.
- `fee_summary` returns text lines, one per member owing more than zero, sorted by amount descending then member id, `"<member_id> <name> <amount>"`, plus a final `"total <amount>"` line (`["total $0.00"]` when nobody owes, so the report is never empty). Lines, not tuples, because the milestone says "report" and the other reports in the package return lines.
- No `effort: high` task: every done-when is arbitrated by unit tests. Coder `opus55` throughout: small, test-driven edits.

## Interfaces

- `shelf/fees.py:18` — `format_cents(cents: int) -> str`. New contract: `format_cents(0) == "$0.00"`, `format_cents(5) == "$0.05"`, `format_cents(1234) == "$12.34"`, `format_cents(123456) == "$1,234.56"`, `format_cents(123456789) == "$1,234,567.89"`, `format_cents(-5) == "-$0.05"`, `format_cents(-123456) == "-$1,234.56"`; non-int or bool → `TypeError`.
- `shelf/fees.py` (new, after `format_cents`) — `parse_cents(text: str) -> int`. Strips surrounding whitespace; grammar `-?\$?(\d{1,3}(,\d{3})*|\d+)(\.\d{2})?`; `parse_cents(format_cents(n)) == n` for every int n; `"-$0.00"` → 0; malformed (`""`, `"$"`, `"12.3"`, `"1,23.00"`, `"abc"`, `"$-1.00"`, `"1.234"`) → `ValueError`.
- `shelf/policy.py:11` — `FEE_CAP_CENTS = 1000` stays (standard cap). New `FEE_CAP_CENTS_BY_KIND = {"standard": 1000, "student": 500, "staff": 1000}` and `fee_cap(kind) -> int` = `FEE_CAP_CENTS_BY_KIND[check_kind(kind)]`.
- `shelf/fees.py:5` — `late_fee_cents(days_late, kind="standard") -> int`; signature unchanged, line 10 becomes `min(billable * policy.daily_fee(kind), policy.fee_cap(kind))`.
- `shelf/fees.py` (new) — `outstanding_cents(desk, member_id, today=None) -> int`: `today = today or desk.today()`; `kind = desk.members.get(member_id).kind` (raises `NotFound` for an unknown member); sum of `loan_fee_cents(loan, today, kind)` over `desk.open_loans(member_id)`.
- `shelf/fees.py` (new) — `fee_summary(desk, today=None) -> list[str]`: for each member in `desk.members` (iterates sorted by id, members.py:45) with `outstanding_cents > 0`, line `f"{member_id} {name} {format_cents(cents)}"`; sorted by cents descending then member id; last line `f"total {format_cents(total)}"`.
- Read-only for this phase: `LoanDesk.open_loans(member_id=None)` loans.py:28, `LoanDesk.today()` loans.py:19, `MemberRegistry.get` members.py:25, `MemberRegistry.__iter__` members.py:45, `Loan.days_late(today)` models.py:62, `tests/helpers.library` helpers.py:41.

## Risks

- Phase 1.2 lands first and moves due dates: T3 tests with hard-coded fee numbers would break. Detection: T4 whole-suite run; mitigation already in T3's done-when (derive expectations from `days_late`).
- The developer picks a different student cap: tests read `policy.fee_cap`, so only the dict entry changes. Detection: none needed beyond T2's tests.
- Someone reads `policy.FEE_CAP_CENTS` as "the cap for everyone" (e.g. phase 1.5's block threshold or 1.6's statements). Detection: grep for `FEE_CAP_CENTS` in T4; the Context note and `fee_cap` docstring say it is the standard cap only.
- `fees → loans` import cycle if T3 imports `LoanDesk` for type hints. Detection: `python -c "import shelf.fees, shelf.loans"` fails / suite errors at import.
- Phase 1.1 not closed when this phase starts (declared dependency). Detection: check GENERATION_PLAN.md status before T1; nothing here touches ISBN code, so a late 1.1 only risks merge noise in tests/helpers.py, which this phase does not edit.
